title: Banjo players he admired when learning
summary: Names the good banjoists of his youth, Preston, Thomas, Kimball, Rene Hall, Danny Barker and others.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Who were some of the best banjo players when you were just coming up, when you were starting to learn? Or who did you like to hear?

Well, they had some real good banjo players after I started learning how to play banjo. Because during that time, Walter Preston, Kit Thomas, and Bocas, they were the kind of banjo players that the fellas started playing a little later on. Because the fellas a little later on started playing the solo banjos. Now, Kimball, used to admire him the way he played because he used to put the banjo behind his neck and play.
Well, now you have a chance, I guess.
Well, I went to lesson with Sales. And Rene Hall was here then.
And Dijon, Ferdinand Dijon, he was here. And there was a little fella named Walter Williams. He was playing banjo. Son, Duh, is Danny Barker.
I don't know if I heard of you.

Yeah, Son, Duh, that's what they called him. Maybe I've heard of him. I haven't seen Danny for so long, you forget about him being from here. And then we had a fine banjo player with us, Harry Faggert.
Harry Faggert, he was across the lake, though.
Well, during them times, they had nothing but good banjo players there.
There wasn't a lot of them.
You remember the time when you had a good wrist and everything. Yeah.
Yeah, them banjo players was out there. Gee whee.
